result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides within a residential context. While basic infrastructure like traffic lights and curb ramps are present, the environment lacks visible dedicated pedestrian signals and features relatively long crossing distances.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the intersection can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb before the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses, featuring a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and street lighting is present, the wide crossing distance and parked cars near the intersection create visibility and exposure risks.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the crosswalk obstruct the sight lines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street near the foreground crosswalk.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway, including parking lanes, increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: The foreground crosswalk spanning the entire width of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a high-visibility zebra crosswalk. While traffic signals are present, the lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals and the relatively wide roadway width increase exposure for people crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where traffic lights are mounted.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: The zebra crosswalk spanning the main roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.
